title: Cavity-Enhanced Chromium Absorber
scientific_hypothesis: A dielectric micro-cavity formed by HfO2/SiO2 layers surrounding a thin Cr layer will trap visible light through multiple internal reflections, enhancing absorption in Cr beyond what a single pass would achieve, while the dielectric stack reflects near-infrared.
design_principle: Optical micro-cavities create resonant states that confine light within a defined region. By placing Cr within a cavity formed by dielectric mirrors, visible light makes multiple passes through Cr, increasing absorption probability. L24 demonstrates micro-cavity enhancement for spectrally selective solar absorbers.
proposed_topology: Air / HfO2 / SiO2 / HfO2 / Cr / SiO2 / HfO2 / SiO2 / Al substrate
design_variables: Top cavity mirror layer thicknesses (HfO2, SiO2 pairs)
Bottom cavity mirror layer thicknesses (HfO2, SiO2 pairs)
soft_objectives: Maximize absorptance in 400-700 nm band through cavity resonance
Achieve resonance peak within visible band
manufacturing_considerations: Total 9 layers including Cr and cavity mirrors
Cavity thickness must be precise for resonance
Cr positioned at field maximum for maximum absorption
L24 supports micro-cavity approach for solar absorbers
theory_basis: Optical Tamm states and micro-cavity resonance
expected_advantages: Resonance can significantly enhance absorption beyond single-pass limit
Fewer Cr layers reduces material cost
known_risks: Resonance may be too narrow for broadband visible absorption
Cavity alignment sensitive to thickness errors
IR reflectance may be compromised by cavity transmission
execution_request_english: Design a planar multilayer stack with air incidence on an aluminum substrate. Stack sequence from air to substrate: two HfO2/SiO2 (Lemarchand) pairs as top mirror, one chromium layer as cavity defect, two HfO2/SiO2 (Lemarchand) pairs as bottom mirror, terminating at aluminum substrate. Total layer count is 9 (4 dielectric pairs + 1 Cr (Rakic-LD) + Al (Rakic-LD) substrate not counted as film layer). Optimize the thickness of the chromium layer and all dielectric layer thicknesses independently to create a resonant cavity. Wavelength range 400-2000 nm. Target: maximize absorptance in 400-700 nm through cavity resonance, maximize reflectance in 700-2000 nm. Normal incidence, unpolarized light.
